A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same vec2vec study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the checklist present only in v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original embedding-translation, attribute-inference, inversion, and ablation results in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds further optimal-transport baseline measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same adapters, shared MLP backbone, discriminators, and adversarial, reconstruction, cycle-consistency, and vector-space-preservation losses. The revised baseline documentation does not change vec2vec.

E1.justification: Both versions use Natural Questions, TweetTopic, MIMIC, and Enron for the same translation and information-extraction tasks. CLIP translation and the out-of-distribution scenarios already appear in v1; v3 adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The naïve and oracle attribute-inference comparators remain. Oracle-aided optimal assignment is renamed optimal transport, retaining Hungarian, Earth Mover’s Distance, Sinkhorn, and Gromov-Wasserstein. v3 makes the CLIP comparison’s use of Gromov-Wasserstein explicit without establishing a comparator addition or removal.

E3.justification: v3 extends OT evaluation to barycentric cosine similarity, which v1 explicitly described as inapplicable. New Appendix B also documents transport-mass ranking, top-1 extraction, and lowest-rank solver selection. Dataset splits, sample counts, model configurations, and vec2vec evaluation settings remain unchanged; additional documentation does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The component-removal experiments and training-data-size study in Tables 8–9 are retained, moving from Appendix C to D. Out-of-distribution tests and inversion examples also remain unchanged. The additional OT cosine entry in Table 8 does not introduce a new ablation question or condition.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors for cosine similarity and rank and select the best of unspecified multiple initializations. v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical procedures. Its additional OT entries follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The comparative evidence expands substantially through previously unavailable OT cosine results in Tables 2, 4, and 6–8. For example, Table 7 newly reports granite-to-gte OT similarity of 0.92 versus vec2vec’s unchanged 0.85, despite poor OT matching. Several OT accuracy and rank values also change: TweetTopic granite-to-gtr rank changes from 400.99 to 398.32. Vec2vec, naïve, information-extraction, and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B defines transport-mass-based rank and a barycentric target embedding used to evaluate OT cosine similarity. This adds a mathematical construction for a previously excluded evaluation, beyond restating the cosine formula. The method’s equations and Strong Platonic Representation Hypothesis remain unchanged; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain unsupervised cross-model text-embedding translation, evidence for the Strong Platonic Representation Hypothesis, and information leakage. The headline 0.92 similarity and perfect-matching claims are retained. The new word-versus-sequence footnote clarifies research positioning without changing the demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: Section 2 replaces categorical inapplicability of correspondence methods with acknowledgment that some support translation without overlapping inputs but struggle empirically. Removing the checklist also removes its explicit connection between GAN instability, long computation, and limited translation quality, although instability and future improvements remain discussed elsewhere.

D1.justification: Appendix B and solver symbols disclose how OT predictions, rankings, top-1 scores, and selected solvers are obtained. Hardware, compute totals, and the code link remain unchanged. Checklist removal drops statements about code documentation and the absence of planned model-weight releases; it does not establish changed resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds eight cited works, including research on ICA geometry, unsupervised word mapping, sentence-embedding comparison, and cross-modal alignment. Sections 2 and 7 refine the relationship to correspondence methods and prior word translation while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the abstract, problem formulation, and related work. A new OT appendix shifts the existing appendix labels, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. The main eight-section narrative and most methodological and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 4, 6, and 7 gain OT cosine columns; Tables 2, 6, and 7 add solver symbols. Appendix table rows are reordered and tables repositioned. Figure 3’s caption is corrected, and Figure 7 moves to a separate final page. All seven figures and nine tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The added OT measurements and Appendix B make the baseline comparison more transparent, while Section 2 corrects an overly categorical dismissal of prior approaches. These provide a modest net improvement without changing the core empirical contribution. The gains are limited by retained broad superiority wording despite high OT cosine scores and the loss of specific checklist caveats.
